question: Your web search subagent calls two MCP tools. One tool returns publication dates as Unix timestamps, and the other returns ISO 8601 strings. The subagent sometimes misreads the Unix timestamps, so the synthesis subagent receives findings in the wrong order of recency. How should you make sure that the web search subagent always works with dates in one format?

options.text: Implement a tool call interception hook that checks each outgoing search call and blocks calls to the tool that returns Unix timestamps.
options.reason: Interception of outgoing calls is for enforcing compliance rules; it changes no tool result, and blocking the tool only removes a research source.

options.text: Add an instruction to the system prompt of the web search subagent that tells it to convert Unix timestamps to ISO 8601.
options.reason: Prompt instructions give only probabilistic compliance; the subagent can still misread a timestamp, while a hook gives a deterministic guarantee.

options.text: Instruct the synthesis subagent to detect and convert the date formats in the findings before it orders them by recency.
options.reason: This relies on prompt instructions, which are probabilistic, and it acts after the web search subagent has already processed the unnormalized results.

options.text: Implement a PostToolUse hook that converts every date in the tool results to ISO 8601 before the web search subagent processes them.
options.reason: PostToolUse hooks intercept tool results and transform them before the model processes them, so normalization of heterogeneous data formats is deterministic.
